ui.scoreDisclaimer: The score is this extension's internal diagnostic value. It is not a prediction of Google or Yandex rankings.

overview.noIssues: No issues found. All base checks passed.

headings.empty: No headings found on the page

links.needsPermission: Network checks need permission to access websites. It is requested once and can be revoked in browser settings.

social.noOg: Open Graph is not configured. Social networks may build the card incorrectly.

content.densityNote: The extension reports actual values and does not impose a target keyword density.

technical.iframeNote: iframe contents are not analyzed — this is an extension limitation.
technical.networkNote: Network checks request robots.txt, sitemap.xml and the headers of the current URL.

settings.title: OnPage SEO Assistant settings
settings.autoRun: Run audit when the popup opens
settings.thresholdNote: Thresholds are guidance, not hard search-engine rules.
settings.mutedNote: Muted rules do not affect the score. List IDs separated by commas, e.g. META-014, IMG-007.

errorsUi.restricted: Audits cannot run on internal browser pages. Open a regular website.
errorsUi.noContentScript: Could not connect to the page. Reload the tab and try again.
errorsUi.noPermission: Permission was not granted — network checks were skipped.

META-001.d: There is no <title> element in <head>. Search engines will generate a snippet headline themselves, usually with a worse result.
META-001.r: Add a <title> with a unique page headline, roughly 30–60 characters.

META-002.d: The <title> element exists but contains no text.
META-002.r: Fill the <title> with a unique headline that reflects the page content.

META-003.d: The title exceeds the recommended threshold. Long titles are often truncated in search results.
META-003.r: Shorten the title to about {max} characters, front-loading the important words.

META-004.d: The title is below the recommended threshold and is likely not descriptive enough.
META-004.r: Expand the title to roughly {min}–{max} characters.

META-005.d: The page has no <meta name="description">. The snippet description will be assembled automatically from page text.
META-005.r: Add a unique page description of roughly {min}–{max} characters.

META-006.d: The description tag is present but its value is empty.
META-006.r: Fill the description with a short, unique summary of the page.

META-007.d: The description exceeds the recommended threshold and will most likely be truncated in the snippet.
META-007.r: Shorten the description to about {max} characters.

META-008.d: There is no <link rel="canonical">. If duplicates exist, the search engine will pick the canonical version itself.
META-008.r: Add <link rel="canonical"> with the absolute URL of the preferred version.

META-009.t: Canonical points to a different URL
META-009.d: The canonical differs from the current page address. That is expected for duplicates and pagination, but a wrong canonical removes the page from the index.
META-009.r: Verify that the canonical really is the preferred version of this page.

META-010.d: Without a viewport tag the page does not adapt to mobile screen widths.

META-011.d: The <html> element has no lang attribute. This affects screen readers and language-version detection.
META-011.r: Add a lang attribute to <html>, e.g. lang="en".

META-012.d: Meta robots contains a noindex directive — the page will not be added to the index.
META-012.r: If the page should be indexed, remove noindex from meta robots.

META-013.d: Meta robots contains nofollow — crawlers will not follow links from this page.
META-013.r: Confirm the crawl restriction is intentional.

META-014.d: Neither <link rel="icon"> nor apple-touch-icon was found.
META-014.r: Add a favicon — it appears in the browser tab and sometimes in search results.

META-015.d: The description is below the recommended threshold and probably does not summarize the page.
META-015.r: Expand the description to roughly {min}–{max} characters.

META-016.d: The document has more than one <title> element. Browsers and crawlers use the first and ignore the rest.

META-017.d: The keywords tag has been ignored by Google for many years. It does no harm but usually adds no value.
META-017.r: The tag can be removed unless internal site systems need it.

META-018.d: The page has more than one canonical tag. On conflict a search engine may ignore both.

META-019.d: A relative canonical is allowed but more often breaks when the protocol or domain changes.
META-019.r: Use an absolute canonical URL including protocol and host.

META-020.d: The hreflang set contains no self-referencing entry for the current URL — a common reason the markup is ignored.
META-020.r: Add an hreflang entry pointing at the current URL.

META-021.d: The hreflang value does not look like a valid language or region code.
META-021.r: Use ISO format: ru, en-US, de-AT or x-default.

META-022.d: No x-default fallback is declared for users who match none of the locales.
META-022.r: Add <link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default"> pointing to the default version.

HEAD-001.d: No first-level heading was found. H1 helps establish the main topic of the document.
HEAD-001.r: Add a single H1 that reflects the page's main content.

HEAD-002.d: An H1 element exists but contains no text.
HEAD-002.r: Fill the H1 with a meaningful heading.

HEAD-003.d: The page has more than one H1. HTML5 allows this, but it makes the main topic harder to determine and often signals markup problems.
HEAD-003.r: Review the structure: one H1 is usually enough, with H2 and below for the rest.

HEAD-004.d: The H1 exceeds {max} characters and is harder for readers to parse.
HEAD-004.r: Shorten the H1 to its essential meaning.

HEAD-005.d: One or more headings contain no text — usually leftover markup or decorative elements.
HEAD-005.r: Remove empty headings or replace them with neutral elements.

HEAD-006.d: The hierarchy is broken: a heading is followed by a level that skips one or more intermediate levels.
HEAD-006.r: Order headings sequentially: H1 → H2 → H3, without gaps.

HEAD-007.d: Several headings share the same text, which weakens the document structure.
HEAD-007.r: Make headings unique within the page.

HEAD-008.d: The heading is in the DOM but not visible to the user (display:none, visibility:hidden or zero size).
HEAD-008.r: Confirm the hiding is intentional, e.g. for accessibility.

HEAD-009.t: H1 is identical to the title
HEAD-009.d: Title and H1 match exactly. Not an error, but a missed chance to cover additional phrasing.
HEAD-009.r: Make H1 and Title complement each other.

HEAD-010.d: There are no second-level subheadings — long text without structure is harder to read.
HEAD-010.r: Split the content into sections with H2.

LINK-001.d: An <a> element with an empty href was found — it points at the current page.
LINK-001.r: Set a valid address or use <button> instead of a link.

LINK-002.d: The link points at "#" and is most likely handled by JavaScript.
LINK-002.r: Use <button> for interactive controls and keep links for navigation.

LINK-003.d: The address starts with javascript:. Crawlers do not follow such links.
LINK-003.r: Replace with a normal href or a <button> with a handler.

LINK-004.d: The link has no text and no image with alt — neither users nor crawlers can tell where it goes.
LINK-004.r: Add link text or an aria-label.

LINK-005.d: The link wraps an image that has no alt, so the anchor text is empty.
LINK-005.r: Add an alt to the image — it becomes the anchor text.

LINK-006.d: Opening in a new tab without noopener gives the target page access to window.opener. Modern browsers protect against this by default, but the attribute is still good practice.
LINK-006.r: Add rel="noopener" (or noopener noreferrer) to such links.

LINK-007.d: Some internal links carry a nofollow attribute. Steering crawl of your own site this way is rarely useful.
LINK-007.r: Check whether nofollow is really needed on internal links.

LINK-008.d: Several links point at one address but use different anchor text.
LINK-008.r: Check whether this hurts clarity; navigation usually benefits from one consistent anchor.

LINK-009.t: Link to http:// from a secure page
LINK-009.d: The page is served over HTTPS but links to the insecure version.
LINK-009.r: Replace http:// with https:// in link addresses.

LINK-010.d: The network check returned a 4xx or 5xx response code.
LINK-010.r: Fix the address or remove the link.

LINK-011.d: The requested address returns a redirect to another URL.
LINK-011.r: Point at the final address directly to remove the extra hop.

LINK-012.d: The anchor exceeds {max} characters and probably contains a whole sentence instead of a meaningful phrase.
LINK-012.r: Shorten the anchor to a short descriptive phrase.

IMG-001.t: Image is missing the ALT attribute
IMG-001.d: The alt attribute is not set. This is an accessibility problem and loses context for image search.
IMG-001.r: Add an alt describing the content. Use alt="" for purely decorative images.

IMG-002.d: The image has alt="". That is correct for decorative elements but wrong for meaningful ones.
IMG-002.r: Confirm the image really is decorative.

IMG-003.d: The alt exceeds {max} characters. Screen readers will announce all of it.
IMG-003.r: Shorten the alt to a brief description.

IMG-004.t: width and height are not set
IMG-004.d: Without explicit dimensions the browser cannot reserve space, which causes layout shift while loading.
IMG-004.r: Set width and height attributes matching the image's aspect ratio.

IMG-005.d: The browser could not fetch the file at the given address.
IMG-005.r: Check the file path and its availability.

IMG-006.t: No lazy loading below the fold
IMG-006.d: The image is below the initial viewport but loads immediately.

IMG-007.d: The image is served as a single file for every screen, including mobile.
IMG-007.r: Add srcset and sizes for responsive delivery.

IMG-008.d: The image is in the DOM but is not shown to the user.
IMG-008.r: Remove unnecessary hidden images — they may still be downloaded.

IMG-009.d: The inline SVG has no <title>, no aria-label and no role="img".
IMG-009.r: Add a <title> inside the SVG or an aria-label on the element.

IMG-010.t: Lazy loading on an above-the-fold image
IMG-010.d: The image is visible immediately but marked loading="lazy", which delays rendering of the main content.

SD-001.d: The page contains no JSON-LD, Microdata or RDFa.
SD-001.r: Add Schema.org markup matching the page type (Article, Product, Organization, etc.).

SD-002.d: A <script type="application/ld+json"> block could not be parsed as JSON — the whole block will be ignored.
SD-002.r: Fix the JSON syntax: trailing commas, unescaped quotes, comments.

SD-003.d: Without an @context of schema.org the markup will not be interpreted.

SD-004.d: The markup object does not declare its entity type.
SD-004.r: Add "@type" with a suitable Schema.org type.

SD-005.d: The same entity type is described by several blocks. That is allowed but often signals conflicting plugins.
SD-005.r: Check whether the blocks duplicate each other with different data.

SD-006.d: Besides JSON-LD the page uses an older markup syntax.
SD-006.r: Google recommends JSON-LD as the preferred format.

SOC-001.d: Without og:title social networks fall back to the title tag or page text.

SOC-002.d: The card description will be assembled automatically and may be irrelevant.

SOC-003.d: Without an image the card is far less noticeable in a feed.
SOC-003.r: Add an og:image of at least 1200×630 pixels.

SOC-004.d: og:url declares the canonical address for sharing.
SOC-004.r: Add <meta property="og:url"> with an absolute URL.

SOC-005.d: The object type is not declared; website is used by default.
SOC-005.r: Set og:type, e.g. article for a post.

SOC-006.d: Without twitter:card the X/Twitter card may render in a reduced form.

SOC-007.d: No og: tags were found on the page. Social networks may build the card incorrectly.
SOC-007.r: Add the basic set: og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url.

SOC-008.d: The sharing address differs from the page's canonical address.
SOC-008.r: Align og:url and canonical to the same value.

CNT-001.d: The page has {n} words of visible text. That is usually not enough for an informational page.
CNT-001.r: Assess whether the text covers the page topic. For catalogues and landing pages a small volume can be normal.

CNT-002.d: Text blocks that are not visually available to the user were found. Some are ordinary tabs and accordions, but hiding text at scale is risky.
CNT-002.r: Verify the hidden text belongs to the interface rather than an attempt to place extra keywords.

CNT-003.d: The word "{term}" occurs {n} times, which is {density}% of the text.
CNT-003.r: Check that the phrasing reads naturally. The extension sets no target density but sharp outliers are worth reviewing.

CNT-004.d: Visible text makes up {ratio}% of the document size.
CNT-004.r: This is an indicative metric. A high markup share often points at heavy templates.

CNT-005.d:
No

element with text was found.
CNT-005.r: Structure text into paragraphs — it improves both readability and parsing.

TECH-001.t: Page is not served over HTTPS
TECH-001.d: The protocol is {protocol}. Browsers mark such pages as not secure.
TECH-001.r: Set up HTTPS and a permanent redirect from http to https.

TECH-002.d: A secure page loads resources over http://. The browser may block them.

TECH-003.d: No <meta charset> was found. Without an explicit charset characters may render incorrectly.
TECH-003.r: Add <meta charset="utf-8"> as the first element in <head>.

TECH-004.d: The document has {n} nodes. A large DOM slows rendering and increases memory use.
TECH-004.r: Reduce depth and element count, especially in long lists.

TECH-005.d: {n} external scripts without async or defer were found — they delay HTML parsing.
TECH-005.r: Add defer or async wherever execution order allows.

TECH-006.d: Unhandled errors were recorded while the page ran. They can break content rendering.
TECH-006.r: Open the browser console and fix the errors.

TECH-007.d: {n} frames were found. Their contents are not part of this audit — an extension limitation.
TECH-007.r: Audit frame contents separately if they matter for indexing.

TECH-008.d: The rule "{rule}" in robots.txt disallows crawling of the current address.
TECH-008.r: If the page should be indexed, adjust robots.txt.

TECH-009.d: The X-Robots-Tag HTTP header contains noindex: {value}.
TECH-009.r: Remove the server-side directive if the restriction is not intended.

TECH-010.d: No sitemap is served at the standard /sitemap.xml address and none is declared in robots.txt.
TECH-010.r: Publish sitemap.xml and declare it in robots.txt with a Sitemap directive.

TECH-011.d: The requested URL passes through {n} redirects before the final address.
TECH-011.r: Reduce the chain to a single hop.

TECH-012.d: robots.txt was not found or returned an error. A missing file does not block crawling, but you lose control over it.
TECH-012.r: Place a robots.txt at the domain root.
